hints.title: Constant Time Minimum Retrieval
hints.text: How can you retrieve the minimum element in constant time during removal without scanning every element?

hints.title: Parallel History of Minimums
hints.text: Pair each value with the minimum observed up to that point, or record each new minimum alongside the regular sequence.

hints.title: Synchronized Minimum Sequence Procedure
hints.text: Maintain an auxiliary sequence for minimums. When pushing a value, also record it if it is less than or equal to the current minimum. When removing an element, if it matches the current minimum, remove it from the auxiliary sequence as well. Top and getMin return the respective tops.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: total number of elements pushed onto stack (at most 3 * 10^4 operations)
complexity.notes: All operations push, pop, top, and getMin run in strictly O(1) time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Scanning the entire stack to find the minimum on every getMin call takes O(N) time. With up to 3 * 10^4 operations, repeated linear scans result in ~9 * 10^8 operations, leading to Time Limit Exceeded.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Maintaining a parallel min-stack uses O(N) auxiliary space to achieve O(1) time across all four operations.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Constant time for all four operations, clean handling of duplicate minimums using <= in push, and zero memory leaks.
